transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Palomar Head Data Platforms), Rajiv Kapoor (CTO), Elena Torres (Security), Jasleen Singh (NLP Lead)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Palomar Health is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment — use cases include clinical triage summarization (short context), and patient history stitching (long context up to ~64k tokens), multilingual outreach (English/Spanish/Tagalog), and secure tool-calling to external EHR connectors. Security and data residency are chief concerns; they'd prefer a private/VPC control plane for PHI. Discussed open models (Mistral, Lama variants, Falcon, Mosaic), quantization tradeoffs, and Redwood's batching and KV cache. Next steps: POC kickoff, perf run, share security docs.

00:00 Speaker: Samira Patel
[00:00] Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira, AE on the Redwood side. Quick intros, then Diego will walk through model choices and deployment options.

00:34 Speaker: Maya Chen
[00:34] Hi Samira, Maya here, heading data platforms. We've got Rajiv and Elena and Jasleen on from the teams. We're trying to figure out where to put inference — hosted for dev, private for prod with PHI. We also want to know how models handle 30k to 60k-ish context for stitching patient notes.

01:02 Speaker: Diego Morales
[01:02] Nice to meet you all. Quick preface: we usually split by workload — short-turn summarization and long-document retrieval style generation. For Palomar, sounds like both. Open models we typically consider: Mistral-7b-style, \"Lama 3\" family, Falcon 40b, Mosaic models — each with different perf and cost points. Note: transcript may say \"Lama\" sometimes — it's Llama family.

01:35 Speaker: Rajiv Kapoor
[01:35] When you say long context, how confident are we at 64k? We have EHR blobs that are 10-20 pages. Latency there is a concern.

01:52 Speaker: Diego Morales
[01:52] Good question. Native 64k context depends on model architecture and tokenization. Some open models are patched for 32k, others 64k experimental. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache and streaming so we can stitch longer context using chunked retrieval and KV cache to avoid recomputing history. Expect tradeoffs: more memory and higher GPU requirements.

02:25 Speaker: Elena Torres
[02:25] Our compliance team is strict. We need KMS integration, audit logs, and preferably private control plane — we can't have PHI hitting a public tenancy. SOC2 is a given. How does Redwood handle encrypted keys and auditability?

02:45 Speaker: Samira Patel
[02:45] We have Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations. We can surface audit logs, role-based access controls, and HSM-backed signing if needed. We'll share the SOC2/ISO packet after this call.

03:06 Speaker: Maya Chen
[03:06] Great. On multilingual, we have outreach in Spanish and Tagalog. Which models handle that out of the box or do we need finetuning?

03:20 Speaker: Diego Morales
[03:20] Some open models (Mosaic and Mistral variants) have decent multilingual coverage; Llama-family models with instruction finetune often do okay, but for Tagalog you may need targeted finetune or retrieval augmentation. Redwood supports fine-tuning workflows in Dedicated/Private but for hosted we often recommend retrieval+tool-calling for consistent outputs.

03:58 Speaker: Jasleen Singh
[03:58] On tool-calling: we need the model to invoke EHR connectors to fetch a patient's latest labs, then summarize and create triage notes. Is function-calling supported? How deterministic is it?

04:12 Speaker: Diego Morales
[04:12] Redwood supports structured function/tool calling in the API — you can define callable schemas. We also offer reranking and safe-fallback policies; for critical workflows we'd recommend canarying the tool-call and adding strict schema validation on the host side. Determinism depends on model and prompt design; smaller models with constrained decodes + n-best rerank can be more consistent.

04:45 Speaker: Rajiv Kapoor
[04:45] Cost is a big one. If we go to Dedicated, what's the rough per-1000-token cost delta vs hosted? Also: burst capacity — during surge with many triage events, can you autoscale?

05:05 Speaker: Samira Patel
[05:05] Dedicated is priced as reserved capacity — unit economics improve for sustained throughput. Hosted per-token is easier to start. Redwood Dedicated supports autoscaling pools and burst lanes; pricing and burst rules are configurable. Diego will follow up with a cost/latency matrix using Palomar sample assumptions.

05:36 Speaker: Diego Morales
[05:36] I will include 8k/32k/64k columns and show GPU sizing. Important note: quantization can reduce GPU memory and cost but may slightly degrade accuracy — for triage that's usually ok, but diagnostics summaries we might prefer FP16 or accuracy-tuned quant profiles.

06:10 Speaker: Elena Torres
[06:10] Any customers running PHI in Private with Redwood — references? Also what about data residency, we host in-west region for CA patients.

06:22 Speaker: Samira Patel
[06:22] Yes, we have references on Private deployments in healthcare customers; we'll share a redacted reference list and provide regional deployment options — can pin to specific cloud regions or on-prem if needed. Data residency can be enforced via VPC and private control plane.

06:45 Speaker: Maya Chen
[06:45] For the POC, we want a realistic perf run: our triage endpoint (short prompts) and a long-document stitch test with 40k context. Can Redwood run both with our sample data?

07:02 Speaker: Diego Morales
[07:02] Absolutely. We usually start with a 48-hour perf run on Dedicated or Private staging — we can run on hosted too for initial numbers but for PHI we'd recommend Private staging. We'll need sample prompts and a small anonymized dataset. Jasleen, could you share that?

07:22 Speaker: Jasleen Singh
[07:22] Yes, I'll scrub and provide a few hundred records and three prompt templates. Expect a little noise in the data.

07:35 Speaker: Rajiv Kapoor
[07:35] Latency numbers matter. If we accept a 300–500ms token generation latency for triage that's okay, but long stitch flows we need throughput more than single-token latency. Does Redwood provide tracing per request?

07:52 Speaker: Samira Patel
[07:52] Redwood Console has per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdowns and you can hook in tracing hooks to your internal observability. You'll be able to see model selection, routing decisions, and in-flight fallbacks.

08:13 Speaker: Elena Torres
[08:13] For security review: SSO, RBAC, session logging, key rotation. Can we integrate with our Okta?

08:25 Speaker: Samira Patel
[08:25] Yes, SSO/SAML with Okta is supported for both Hosted and Private; RBAC is more granular on Dedicated/Private. We'll add the integration guide to the materials.

08:42 Speaker: Diego Morales
[08:42] Quick technical aside: for the long context stitching we recommend either a model natively supporting 64k or a retrieval-first approach combined with KV cache. Retrieval chunk sizes, overlap, and embedding model selection all matter. For embeddings we can run internal benchmarks but often use a smaller dedicated embedding model to save token costs.

09:10 Speaker: Maya Chen
[09:10] Question on model ops — how do you do rollouts, if we pin a model version and then Redwood publishes a new variant, do we control the rollout?

09:22 Speaker: Samira Patel
[09:22] Yes, you can pin model versions, use canary or A/B rollouts, and Redwood supports automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a new model fails SLOs. Rollouts are part of the Console controls.

09:40 Speaker: Jasleen Singh
[09:40] For Tagalog support, if we need domain-specific behavior, can we host a fine-tuned variant in Dedicated/Private? How does that interact with model routing?

09:55 Speaker: Diego Morales
[09:55] You can bring your finetuned checkpoint and Redwood can host it in Dedicated/Private. Model routing policies can route particular customer IDs or routes to those finetuned variants. We also support multi-model ensembles for reranking if you want a smaller model to propose candidates and a larger model to finalise.

10:20 Speaker: Rajiv Kapoor
[10:20] Any caveats on on-prem deployments? We have legacy infra with limited GPU inventory.

10:31 Speaker: Samira Patel
[10:31] On-prem works but depends on your GPU fleet — some models require A100-class memory for large contexts. We offer an on-prem package and can help size nodes. For limited GPUs we often recommend quantized models or offloading larger workloads to Dedicated with VPC peering.

10:52 Speaker: Elena Torres
[10:52] About logging: can we keep full logs in our S3 with lifecycle policies and ensure deletion after X days?

11:05 Speaker: Diego Morales
[11:05] Yes, Redwood can push audit logs to your S3 or SIEM; retention and lifecycle you control. We'll include a log flow diagram in the follow-up.

11:25 Speaker: Maya Chen
[11:25] Sounds good. Anything else we should consider for accuracy regressions during quantization?

11:35 Speaker: Diego Morales
[11:35] We recommend a small eval suite tied to production prompts. Redwood Optimize can monitor regressions and alert if quality drops. Also try 4-bit vs 8-bit quant profiles; measure on your eval set.

11:58 Speaker: Samira Patel
[11:58] Let's recap next steps. Diego will produce the cost/latency spreadsheet and a recommended model shortlist for short vs long flows. I'll send SOC2 and the private deployment checklist. Palomar will send sample prompts/data and confirm compliance constraints. We aim to kick off a POC on 2026-11-09.

12:22 Speaker: Rajiv Kapoor
[12:22] That works for us. Quick off-topic: any prebuilt connectors for Epic/Cerner?

12:34 Speaker: Diego Morales
[12:34] We have pattern templates and community connectors; for Epic/Cerner usually customers bring the integrations but we provide the tooling and auth patterns. We'll add notes in the follow-up.

12:50 Speaker: Jasleen Singh
[12:50] I'll try to get the anonymized dataset by Thursday.

13:00 Speaker: Samira Patel
[13:00] Thank you everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present (Lama vs Llama, K V cache written as KV cache or K-V cache, \"quant\" shorthand, overheard crosstalk). Speakers sometimes labeled generically in the raw export; I've mapped names when clear.
